title: Add per-camera `subjects` allowlist to motion_gate_thresholds.json + gate.py routing so face-level cameras (FRONT/BACK) suppress vehicles and never drop solo-person detections
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-18)
trigger: Operator 2026-09-18 (verbatim): 'Front door outside is specifically set at face level and it's specifically supposed to get people. I don't even care if it captures a vehicle. Back door inside is the same thing. Front door outside and back door inside are specifically set up to get the best images of people. I don't want, well also in animals, but I don't want any vehicles captured from front door outside or back door inside. What's an elegant way to make that happen?' Investigation: Front Door Outside camera (192.168.1.39) sent 266 webhook POSTs in the last 24h; only 20 proceeded through the pipeline (7.5% pass rate). The last successful FRONT person alert in the entire log was 2026-09-14 11:37:01 (4 days ago). Today, 09:59:56 had a `top_class=person top_confidence=0.61 reason=high_conf_person_not_vehicle` drop -- a real person was detected and then explicitly suppressed because no vehicle was in the mix. The rule lives at infra/gate.py:752-757 (catchall Rule 5) and was locked into a v0.5.0 release to prevent 225 'bench = vehicle' false positives on perimeter cameras. The fix needs to preserve that protection for OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR/OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR/OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE/OUTSIDE_FRONT_POWER while making FRONT and BACK suppress vehicles and route solo-person to the person pipeline.
background: Current state in /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2/infra/gate.py:752-757 is a hard-coded catchall: if YOLO finds any high-confidence detection but no vehicle in the bbox mix, the gate returns ('none', top_class, top_confidence, 'high_conf_<class>_not_vehicle'). The rule is correct for perimeter/driveway cameras where solo-person detection usually means a person walking past the fence line. It is wrong for entry-level cameras where solo-person IS the primary signal. The v0.5.0 release that locked this rule in was a global change; it cannot be undone without re-introducing the 225 false-positive problem on OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR. The clean fix is to make subjects a per-camera config value in config/motion_gate_thresholds.json (which already carries per-camera vehicle/person thresholds and gate_enabled flags). The gate loads the camera's threshold dict at /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2/infra/gate.py:514 via _load_thresholds_config().get(camera_name). Adding a 'subjects' key in that dict is a natural extension -- no new file, no new env var, no global mode flag. The default when 'subjects' is missing is the current vehicle-priority behavior (backward compatible). Cameras that want different behavior add 'subjects': ['person', 'animal'] (or any subset) and the gate routes accordingly.
goal: FRONT and BACK cameras (config keys in motion_gate_thresholds.json) get a 'subjects': ['person', 'animal'] entry. Their gate routes solo-person and solo-animal to the person/animal pipeline (not to vehicle, not to suppression). Vehicle detections on these cameras are silently dropped at the gate with reason 'top_class_vehicle_not_in_subjects'. Mixed person+vehicle detections on these cameras route to person (since vehicle is not in subjects). All other cameras keep current behavior unchanged. After the change: FRONT/BACK person alerts proceed normally; a solo-person alert at 0.61 confidence (like the 09:59:56 case) is logged as `proceeded classification=people` instead of `dropped reason=high_conf_person_not_vehicle`.

operator_guarantees.no_residue: After all stories land: config/motion_gate_thresholds.json has 'subjects' keys for FRONT and BACK only (4 other cameras omit it). infra/gate.py reads the per-camera subjects value at the same place it already reads per-camera thresholds (line 514-546 region). No new env var is introduced. No global MOTION_GATE_V2 toggle is flipped. The catchall at line 752-757 is REPLACED with a per-camera subjects check; the literal string 'high_conf_<class>_not_vehicle' no longer appears in the codebase.
operator_guarantees.behavior: Per-camera routing rules after the change: (a) FRONT: solo-person@conf>=0.35 -> person pipeline; solo-animal@conf>=0.35 -> animal pipeline; any vehicle -> suppressed with reason 'top_class_vehicle_not_in_subjects'; mixed person+vehicle -> person pipeline. (b) BACK: same as FRONT. (c) OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR/OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR/OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE/OUTSIDE_FRONT_POWER: subjects default (no key) -> current behavior preserved exactly: vehicle in mix wins; no vehicle in mix + solo person/other -> current catchall suppression for non-person classes; solo person routes to person pipeline (existing US-050a behavior).
operator_guarantees.no_regression: After the change: scripts/smoke_alert_native.py exits 0. The /alert webhook route returns HTTP 200 for all cameras. Existing US-046b NIGHT_SUPPRESS behavior (operator 2026-09-15) still gates night-time vehicle false-positives on OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR. Existing US-045f animal pipeline still routes recognized animals to TG#3 with MegaDescriptor cosine. Per-class thresholds in motion_gate_thresholds.json (vehicle=0.5, person=0.35 on FRONT/BACK) remain unchanged.
operator_guarantees.auditability: The motion_gate log line (existing format: 'motion_gate: classification=... top_class=... top_confidence=... reason=... elapsed=...ms') gains a new reason value 'top_class_<class>_not_in_subjects' for FRONT/BACK camera detections that fall outside the camera's subjects. Existing reason values ('mixed_vehicle_wins', 'high_conf_person_not_vehicle', 'no_class', 'class_below_threshold', 'class_not_in_keep', 'gate_disabled_*') remain unchanged. Operators tail-grepping daemon.log see the same log shape, with new reason strings only on FRONT/BACK.
operator_guarantees.config_drift_safe: If a future operator adds a camera but forgets to set 'subjects', the camera falls back to the default behavior (vehicle-priority). This is documented in the JSON _comment and in infra/gate.py:load_thresholds() docstring. There is no implicit 'subjects: []' that would drop everything -- missing key = current behavior.

The script: (a) imports infra.gate.load_thresholds for FRONT, BACK, OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR; asserts FRONT.subjects == {'person', 'animal'} and BACK == same and OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR has no 'subjects' key. (b) Calls the gate function with synthetic detection tuples mimicking: solo-person on FRONT, solo-vehicle on FRONT, mixed person+vehicle on FRONT, solo-person on OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR (current behavior). Asserts the routing outputs match the spec above.
shipping_definition.no_fallback: If the JSON file fails to parse (broken syntax) the gate raises a clean ConfigError (existing behavior). If 'subjects' is set to an empty list, the gate logs a warning ('subjects is empty -- all detections on this camera will be suppressed') and routes accordingly. There is no silent fallback to the old behavior when the operator explicitly opts out of all subjects.
shipping_definition.branch_hygiene: Each story lands on its own code/v2-055<letter>-<slug> branch, ff-merges into main before kanban_done. No uncommitted scratch files. Local main MUST NOT fall behind origin after the change is deployed.

stories.notes: Replace the existing Rule 5 catchall (infra/gate.py:752-757, the `if vehicle_top is not None` / `return ('none', ..., 'high_conf_<class>_not_vehicle')` block) with a per-camera subjects check. The new logic: (1) resolve camera_subjects from the per-camera threshold dict via load_thresholds() (extend the return shape to include 'subjects' if present; default to None when absent). (2) If camera_subjects is None, run the OLD catchall verbatim so OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR/OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR/etc. behavior is unchanged. (3) If camera_subjects is set and top_class is not in it, return ('none', top_class, top_confidence, f'top_class_{top_class}_not_in_subjects'). (4) If camera_subjects is set and 'vehicle' is in it AND vehicle_top is in the bbox mix, run the existing mixed_vehicle_wins rule. (5) If camera_subjects is set and 'vehicle' is NOT in it AND vehicle_top is in the mix, suppress vehicle (return 'none' with reason 'top_class_vehicle_not_in_subjects'). (6) If camera_subjects is set and no vehicle in mix, top detection wins if it's in subjects. The new 'subjects' key flows through load_thresholds() alongside vehicle/person thresholds. Do NOT introduce a new env var. Do NOT touch the V2 mode (MOTION_GATE_V2). The line numbers given are approximate; locate the actual Rule 5 block by grep.
